alternative_reading: Boundary limitations are inherited only when the boundary is an exact premise of a support entry or determines a reason or gap for the asserted claim; in b2 neither holds, so inherited_limitations = {}. This reading has to treat the standalone 'boundary limitations' term as subordinate to the later clauses, which the text does not say, so it is not adopted.
primary_reading: Yes. 'boundary limitations' is a standalone, unqualified member of the section 8.1 union, and section 7 requires every accept or downgrade result to preserve the boundary grounding status and its limitations; the exclusion sentence covers only 'unrelated failed findings', and a supported boundary is neither failed nor unrelated. inherited_limitations = {(mapping-1, L-ts-no-issuer-signature-check)}.
question: Section 8.1 lists 'boundary limitations' as an unconditional term of the inherited_limitations union and section 7 says an accept or downgrade result 'MUST preserve the boundary grounding status and its limitations'. In b2 the boundary is supported but is not a premise of any support entry and the only reason (E_MISSING_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE) has 'source: none'. Are the boundary limitations still inherited?
